analyst_view.overall: Early view: two big clubs in a bad way. Newcastle under Matthias Jaissle were booed off after losing at home to Everton, and Manchester United are in the relegation zone, without a league win since August, with Michael Carrick expected to stay for now. United also play Sporting in the Champions League on 25 November and have a long injury list, including Benjamin Sesko, Marcus Rashford and Carlos Baleba.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.2 goals. I agree: United have conceded more than any side in Europe's top five leagues in all competitions and just drew 4-4 with Villa, which points up, but Newcastle's attack has been flat and their first shot on target against Everton came after 85 minutes, which points down. Those two forces roughly cancel out.

corners.text: The site has 10.0 corners. I agree: Newcastle attack down the flanks with Anthony Elanga and Harvey Barnes, and United will press forward if they fall behind. No strong reason to move the figure.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.5 cards. I lean slightly higher: Newcastle defend man-to-man, which brings fouls, and Jacob Ramsey picked up two yellows in 86 seconds against Everton. With both clubs under pressure and the crowd on edge, five bookings is quite possible.

shots.text: The site has 29.8 shots, 16.2 of them for United. I lean lower: United are without Sesko and probably Rashford, and Newcastle have created very little lately. A messy game, but not one with 30 shots.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.7 shots on target. I lean lower because Newcastle's finishing has been poor (no shots on target in the first half against Everton) and United's attack is thinned out. United do concede plenty, so I would not go much lower than eight.
